channel.title: Walking with Jesus
channel.description: Morning, midday, and evening reflections on His life, teaching, and love.

item.title: Fear Not, Little Flock
item.description: A Saturday midday among the errands and the lists, with one sentence from Jesus about the Father's heart that changes how the whole list feels.

item.title: Sir, We Would See Jesus
item.description: A Saturday morning with a handful of strangers who came a long way with one simple request, and the surprising answer Jesus gave about seeing Him.

item.title: I Go to Prepare a Place
item.description: A Friday evening in the upper room, where Jesus speaks to troubled hearts about a Father's house with room in it, and a promise that He will come back for His own.

item.title: But Whom Say Ye That I Am?
item.description: A Friday midday pause with the question Jesus asked His friends far from home, the one question nobody else can answer for you.

item.title: Not Far from the Kingdom
item.description: A Friday morning with a scribe who asked Jesus the biggest question of all, got an answer about love, and heard the gentlest words a seeker could hope for.

item.title: Behold Thy Mother
item.description: A Thursday evening at the foot of the cross, where Jesus, in His hardest hour, looks down and makes sure the people He loves will not be left alone.

item.title: And Took Her by the Hand
item.description: A Thursday midday in Simon's house in Capernaum, where a woman lies sick in a back room, someone finally mentions her, and Jesus comes close enough to lift her up.

item.title: Save Jesus Only
item.description: A Thursday morning on the mountain of transfiguration, where the glory fades, a hand touches frightened shoulders, and the disciples look up to find Jesus only.

item.title: With Desire I Have Desired
item.description: A Wednesday evening at the table with Jesus on the night before the cross, and the quiet surprise that He actually wanted to be there with them.

item.title: One Thing I Know
item.description: A Wednesday midday with the man born blind in John 9, who couldn't answer every question but knew what Jesus had done, and who was found again after he was pushed out.

item.title: I Saw Thee
item.description: A Wednesday morning with Nathanael under the fig tree, and the quiet comfort of being seen by Jesus before anyone calls your name.

item.title: The Things Which Belong unto Thy Peace
item.description: A Tuesday evening with Jesus on the hill above Jerusalem, weeping over a city, and gently asking what made for peace in your day.

item.title: Neither Do I Condemn Thee
item.description: A Tuesday midday with Jesus stooping in the dust, the stones going down one by one, and the voice that finally speaks last.

item.title: Moved with Compassion
item.description: A Tuesday morning with Jesus looking out at a tired crowd, and what He actually feels when He sees us.

item.title: Abide in Me
item.description: A Monday evening with the true vine, for anyone who spent the day straining to produce and feels wrung out by nightfall.

item.title: Until Seventy Times Seven
item.description: A Monday midday with Peter's question about forgiveness, the king who forgave a debt no one could pay, and the small grudges we pick up before lunch.

item.title: He Put His Hands Again
item.description: A Monday morning with the blind man of Bethsaida, the healing that came in two touches, and a Jesus who doesn't leave us half-seeing.

item.title: Because I Am Good
item.description: A Sunday evening with the workers hired at the eleventh hour, for anyone who feels late, overlooked, or behind on the week ahead.

item.title: The Sabbath Was Made for Man
item.description: A Sunday midday walk through the grain fields with Jesus, hungry disciples, and a day of rest that was always meant as a gift.

item.title: And Yet There Is Room
item.description: A Sunday morning with the parable of the great supper, the polite excuses we all make, and a table that still isn't full.

item.title: In No Wise Cast Out
item.description: A Saturday evening with one of Jesus' plainest promises, for anyone who wonders whether they've worn out their welcome with God.

item.title: And Took a Towel
item.description: A Saturday midday with the laundry and the dishes, and the night Jesus got up from supper to wash dusty feet.

item.title: Jesus Rejoiced in Spirit
item.description: A Saturday morning with the seventy coming home full of stories, and the moment Luke tells us Jesus Himself was glad.

item.title: It Is I; Be Not Afraid
item.description: A Friday evening on a dark sea, where the disciples row against the wind all night, Jesus comes walking toward them in the fourth watch, and one sinking man finds a hand already reaching for him.

item.title: Give Me to Drink
item.description: A Friday midday at the well with Jesus, tired from the road, asking a woman for water and offering her something that never runs dry.

item.title: Till She Find It
item.description: A Friday morning with the woman who lights a lamp and sweeps the whole house for one lost coin, and what that says about how God looks for us.

item.title: Weep Not
item.description: A Thursday evening at the gate of Nain, where Jesus meets a widow's grief she never asked Him to touch, stops the procession, and gives her son back.

item.title: God Be Merciful to Me
item.description: A Thursday midday with the shortest prayer in the parable of the Pharisee and the publican, and the man who went home justified.

item.title: What Seek Ye?
item.description: A Thursday morning with the first words Jesus speaks in John's Gospel, a simple question that is still the best way to begin a day.

item.title: He Knoweth Not How
item.description: A Wednesday evening with Jesus' small parable of the seed that grows while the farmer sleeps, and why you can lay down today's unfinished work and rest.

item.title: Not One of Them Is Forgotten
item.description: A midweek midday with five cheap sparrows, the hairs on your head, and the quiet promise that God has not lost track of you.

item.title: At Thy Word
item.description: A Wednesday morning with Simon's empty boat on the Lake of Gennesaret, and the one small "nevertheless" that changed his whole life.

item.title: I Have Prayed for Thee
item.description: A Tuesday evening with Peter at the Last Supper, where Jesus tells him he will stumble and, in the same breath, that He has already prayed for him, and what that means for the places you fell short today.

item.title: O Woman, Great Is Thy Faith
item.description: A midday reflection on the Canaanite mother who kept asking when heaven seemed quiet, and the three-word prayer that is always enough.

item.title: Ye Are the Salt of the Earth
item.description: A Tuesday morning with one small word from the Sermon on the Mount, and the quiet difference a little salt makes in an ordinary day.

item.title: Thou Art Loosed
item.description: A Monday evening with the woman bent over for eighteen years, the one Jesus saw, called, touched, and set straight, and what He might want to lift off your shoulders tonight.

item.title: For Joy Thereof
item.description: A Monday midday with the treasure in the field and the pearl of great price, and the joy that makes letting go feel like gain.

item.title: Founded Upon a Rock
item.description: A Monday morning with the wise and foolish builders, and the quiet work of digging deep before the week's weather comes.

item.title: One Thing Is Needful
item.description: A Sunday evening in Bethany with Martha and Mary, where Jesus says Martha's name twice, gently, and points a worried heart toward the one thing that won't be taken away.

item.title: Be Opened
item.description: A Sunday midday with the deaf man in the Decapolis, whom Jesus took aside from the crowd, touched in a language he could understand, and sighed over before He said, Ephphatha.

item.title: As His Custom Was
item.description: A Sunday morning in the synagogue at Nazareth, where Jesus opened the scroll and said the good news was happening today.

item.title: When the Doors Were Shut
item.description: A Saturday evening reflection on the first Easter evening, when the disciples sat behind locked doors and Jesus came and stood in the midst of them, showed them His wounds, and said, "Peace be unto you."

item.title: Thou Hast Kept the Good Wine
item.description: A Saturday midday at a village wedding in Cana, where the wine ran out, a mother brought the problem to Jesus, and He saved the best for last.

item.title: Jesus Beholding Him Loved Him
item.description: A Saturday morning with the man who ran to Jesus — and the look of love that came before the hardest word He would hear.

item.title: When the Even Was Come
item.description: A Friday evening reflection on Joseph of Arimathea, who stepped out of hiding on the darkest Friday of all and gave Jesus his own tomb, and on the faithful love that keeps going when it looks like everything is over.

item.title: Help Thou Mine Unbelief
item.description: A Friday midday with a father who brought Jesus half a faith and a whole heart — and found that the honest prayer was enough to bring to Him.

item.title: I Am the Way
item.description: A Friday morning with Jesus' clear word to troubled hearts — you do not have to invent the path; He is the Way, and He walks it with you into this day.

item.title: When the Sun Was Setting
item.description: A Thursday evening at the door of Peter's house in Capernaum, where a whole town carried its sick to Jesus at sundown, and He laid His hands on every one of them.

item.title: Wilt Thou Be Made Whole?
item.description: A Thursday midday at the pool of Bethesda, where a man had waited thirty-eight years — and Jesus asked the one question that still finds us in the middle of an unfinished day.

item.title: I Have Overcome the World
item.description: A Thursday morning with Jesus' steady word — trouble is real, and so is His victory; take heart and walk with Him into this day.

item.title: Lovest Thou Me?
item.description: A Wednesday evening by a charcoal fire on the shore of Galilee, where Jesus restores Peter after his worst failure with one gentle question asked three times.

item.title: She Cast In All She Had
item.description: A Wednesday midday with the poor widow at the temple treasury, the Jesus who notices small and hidden offerings, and the One who was about to give everything.

item.title: I Am the Light of the World
item.description: A Wednesday morning with Jesus' claim that He is the light — follow Him, and you will not walk this day in darkness.

item.title: I Am the Good Shepherd
item.description: A Tuesday evening with Jesus's words about the Good Shepherd — the One who knows His sheep by name, stays when others run, and lays down His life so you can rest without fear.

item.title: He Saw a Man Sitting at the Tax Booth
item.description: A Tuesday midday with Matthew at his desk, the Jesus who calls people in the middle of their workday, and a table full of the wrong guests.

item.title: I Will Give You Rest
item.description: A Tuesday morning with Jesus' open invitation to the weary — come as you are, take His yoke, and find the rest that Monday could not give you.

item.title: She Loved Much
item.description: A Monday evening at a Pharisee's dinner table, where a woman everyone had already judged found that Jesus saw her, forgave her, and sent her home in peace.

item.title: Where Are the Nine?
item.description: A Monday midday with the ten lepers Jesus healed, and the one who turned back to say thank You.

item.title: Speak the Word Only
item.description: A Monday morning with the centurion who trusted Jesus from a distance, and what that means for the things we can't reach today.

item.title: Not As I Will
item.description: A Sunday evening in Gethsemane, where Jesus brought His heaviest night to the Father and showed us how to pray when the week ahead feels like too much.

item.title: Go, and Do Thou Likewise
item.description: A Sunday midday with the Good Samaritan, and the neighbor who is usually right in front of us.

item.title: To Whom Shall We Go?
item.description: A Sunday morning with Peter, on the day the crowd walked away and Jesus turned to the few who stayed.

item.title: Jesus Wept
item.description: A Saturday evening at the tomb of Lazarus, where the One who was about to fix everything stopped first to cry with His friends.

item.title: Let the Little Children Come
item.description: A Saturday midday with the disciples guarding the door, a Savior who was indignant on behalf of the small, and the open arms that still welcome us.

item.title: Someone Did Touch Me
item.description: A Saturday morning in a pressing crowd, with a woman who hoped to stay hidden and a Savior who stopped everything to call her daughter.

item.title: Lord, Remember Me
item.description: A Friday evening beside a dying thief who had nothing left to offer, and the one-line prayer Jesus answered with a promise.

item.title: While He Was Still Far Off
item.description: A Friday midday pause with the son on the long road home, rehearsing his apology, and the father who couldn't wait for him to finish it.

item.title: When Jesus Saw Their Faith
item.description: A Friday morning on a crowded roof in Capernaum, with four friends who would not stop at the door and a man who couldn't walk to Jesus on his own.

item.title: Stay With Us, for It Is Toward Evening
item.description: A Thursday evening with Cleopas and his friend on the road to Emmaus — the simple invitation that opened their eyes, and still opens ours.

item.title: Consider the Lilies
item.description: A Thursday midday pause for the part of you that's already running numbers on tomorrow. Jesus points at a field of flowers and tells you something about your Father.

item.title: I Want To. Be Made Clean.
item.description: A Thursday morning with the man who knelt in the dust and wondered whether Jesus would even want him. Jesus answers with a touch before He answers with a word.

item.title: He Came to Jesus by Night
item.description: A Wednesday evening with Nicodemus, a careful man with big questions who came to Jesus after dark. For anyone who still has more questions than answers.

item.title: Today I Must Stay at Your House
item.description: A Wednesday midday with a short man in a sycamore tree. Jesus doesn't wait for Zacchaeus to clean up before He invites Himself over, and He doesn't wait for you either.

item.title: In the Fourth Watch
item.description: A Wednesday morning on a wind-tossed lake with Peter. Jesus comes in the last dark hours before sunrise, speaks into the fear, and holds out His hand to anyone who starts to sink.

item.title: Peace! Be Still!
item.description: An evening on the Sea of Galilee, a storm that came out of nowhere, and a Savior asleep in the boat. For the nights when you wonder if He cares.

item.title: What Are These Among So Many?
item.description: A Tuesday midday with a boy's packed lunch on a Galilean hillside. When what you have looks far too small for what the day is asking, Jesus says, bring it here.

item.title: What Do You Want Me to Do for You?
item.description: A Tuesday morning beside the Jericho road with blind Bartimaeus. Jesus stops for the one the crowd tried to hush, and asks a question worth carrying into the day.

item.title: He Took a Towel
item.description: A Monday evening at the supper table in John 13. Before you lie down with the dust of the day still on you, let Jesus kneel and wash what you carried in.

item.title: He Sat Down by the Well
item.description: A Monday midday with the woman at Jacob's well. She came at noon to avoid being seen, and found Someone who saw everything and stayed anyway.

item.title: At Your Word
item.description: A Monday morning with Peter at the shoreline. After a night of empty nets, Jesus asks for one more try — and the whole week can begin on His word instead of yesterday's results.

item.title: Your Faithfulness Every Night
item.description: Sunday evening does not need one more achievement. Psalm 92 invites a quieter close — giving thanks, and proclaiming God’s faithfulness into the night.

item.title: Remain in Me
item.description: Sunday midday can drift back into self-effort. Jesus offers a simpler way — stay connected to Him like a branch to the vine, where fruit grows from nearness, not strain.

item.title: Seek the Things Above
item.description: Sunday morning lifts your eyes. Colossians reminds the raised-with-Christ that the first direction of the day is upward — where Jesus is, and where your true life is kept.

item.title: In Peace I Will Lie Down
item.description: Saturday evening does not need a perfect ending before you can rest. Psalm 4 invites a quieter trust — lying down in peace because the Lord alone makes you dwell in safety.

item.title: Beside Still Waters
item.description: Saturday midday can still feel hurried even when the calendar softens. Psalm 23 invites a tired heart to be led beside still waters — where the Shepherd restores what the week has spent.

item.title: He Who Keeps You Will Not Slumber
item.description: Friday evening invites a different kind of trust — not that you will stay awake to manage everything, but that the Lord who keeps you never nods off.

item.title: Come Away and Rest Awhile
item.description: Friday midday often finds us tired and unfinished. In Mark 6 Jesus invites worn disciples to step aside with Him — not after everything is done, but while the crowd still presses.

item.title: When I Awake, I Am Still with You
item.description: Friday morning does not begin with you finding God. Psalm 139 says something quieter and kinder — you wake, and He is already there.

item.title: Peace I Leave With You
item.description: As Thursday evening settles, Jesus does not offer the world’s thin calm. He leaves His own peace — a gift that steadies troubled and fearful hearts.

item.title: One Thing Is Needed
item.description: Midday often multiplies tasks and noise. In Luke 10 Jesus gently redirects a busy heart toward the one thing that holds — Himself.

item.title: He Goes Before You
item.description: Thursday does not ask you to invent the day alone. Deuteronomy promises a Lord who walks ahead — present, faithful, and already at work in what you cannot yet see.

item.title: Come to the Waters
item.description: Isaiah’s morning invitation is not a pep talk — it is a welcome to thirsty people. Grace still meets us where we are empty, and Jesus still says come.

item.title: Be Our Arm Every Morning
item.description: Isaiah teaches a simple morning prayer — asking God not for a private escape from Tuesday, but for His strength to meet whatever the day actually holds.

item.title: Before the Day Crowds In
item.description: Mark shows Jesus rising early to pray — not to impress heaven, but to meet the Father before the day’s noise arrives. Monday can begin that way too.

item.title: Very Early on the First Day
item.description: Before the week asks anything of you, the Gospels open Sunday with a quiet fact — disciples walking toward a tomb, and a risen Lord who had already gone ahead.

item.title: As Sure as the Dawn
item.description: Hosea invites a tired heart not to invent its own morning, but to press on toward a God whose coming is as reliable as the light that finds the sky.

item.title: Give Us This Day
item.description: Before the calendar fills every pocket of attention, Jesus teaches a simpler morning prayer — asking the Father for today’s bread, not yesterday’s regret or tomorrow’s dread.

item.title: The Sunrise Shall Visit Us
item.description: Zechariah’s song names a mercy that does not wait for us to climb — the sunrise of God’s tender kindness visiting us from on high in Jesus.

item.title: Joy Comes with the Morning
item.description: Psalm 30 does not deny the night — it promises that weeping is not the last word, and that morning can carry a joy God Himself restores.

item.title: In the Morning I Watch
item.description: Psalm 5 offers a quiet morning practice — not only speaking to God, but preparing our hearts and watching for Him with trust.

item.title: Morning by Morning He Awakens
item.description: Before we speak into the day, Isaiah 50 offers a quieter gift — an ear awakened by God, ready to hear mercy and learn trust.

item.title: Satisfy Us in the Morning
item.description: Before the day asks for productivity, Psalm 90 asks for something deeper — a heart filled with God’s steadfast love at dawn.

item.title: Let Me Hear in the Morning
item.description: Before the day fills with noise, Psalm 143 asks for one first word — God’s steadfast love spoken into the quiet of dawn.

item.title: Come and Have Breakfast
item.description: At daybreak by the sea, Jesus welcomes tired disciples with a fire, a meal, and a mercy that arrives before they have a plan.

item.title: While It Was Still Dark
item.description: Mary comes to the tomb before sunrise — and finds that Jesus meets us in the grey hour when hope still feels unfinished.

item.title: New Every Morning
item.description: Before the day fills up, a quiet word from Lamentations — mercies that do not run out, and a Savior who meets us at dawn.

item.title: Stay With Us
item.description: Evening light on the Emmaus road — recognition, burning hearts, and the joy of remaining with the risen Jesus.

item.title: Take My Yoke
item.description: Midday rest for the weary — Jesus’ invitation in Matthew 11 to exchange our heavy loads for His gentle yoke.

item.title: Come and See
item.description: Jesus’ gentle invitation in John 1 — curiosity, encounter, and the beginning of discipleship.
